success_patterns: Several answers came straight from a verbatim archive or flashcard hit. In StudyStack text the clue is followed by a comma and the answer in caps ('...EMOTIONAL IN EFFECT & IMPROVISATIONAL IN NATURE, RHAPSODY'; '...UNESCO IN PARIS, AND LINCOLN CENTER, HENRY MOORE'). In TriviaBistro dumps the clue appears after a category label ('MUSIC VIDEOS: ...'). Rule 3 already covers the general case.

A quote-only clue (the slogan 'Tippecanoe and Tyler too') was resolved to the single person the passages tie to it (William Henry Harrison), not to the slogan, the campaign or the running mate named in it. Rule 1 does not cover this case.

A list of character names was resolved to the shared TV series, and a multi-detail descriptive clue was resolved to the one person that recurs across passage titles (Jesse Owens, Henry Moore). Both are already covered.
Final answers were bare and short ('Bull Moose', 'pomegranate', 'Scream', 'Henry Moore'), with no category words, no repeated clue words and no extra descriptors. This is already covered by Rule 4.
Where the context was mostly noise (the Scream/Creed passage), the agent anchored on the few passages that matched the clue's distinctive details and ignored the irrelevant hits.

patch.reasoning: Most successes confirm rules the skill already has. The one pattern not yet encoded is the quote-only clue: a famous slogan, motto, lyric or catchphrase given alone, with no 'this'. The agent answered with the person it identifies, which was correct. A short addition to Rule 1 makes that explicit. A second short addition names the all-caps 'clue, ANSWER' flashcard layout under Rule 3, so the answer is read off the end of the clue. Both are minimal and low-risk, given that broad rule additions were rejected in earlier steps.

edits.target: - Jokes, asides and filler in the clue ('(If I eat it, can I hear the ocean?)', 'Need help in this subject? Call up...') are decoration.
edits.content: - A clue that is only a quoted slogan, motto, lyric or catchphrase ('"Tippecanoe and Tyler too"') asks WHO or WHAT it belongs to. Answer with the single person (or named thing) the passages tie to it, here the candidate it promoted ('William Henry Harrison'), not the slogan, the campaign, the running mate named inside it or the song. Take the entity that recurs across the passage titles.

edits.target: - Archive lines may also be formatted 'CATEGORY | clue text | answer'.
edits.content: - Flashcard sites such as StudyStack often print the clue and its answer in one all-caps run, with the answer as the last item after a comma ('...EMOTIONAL IN EFFECT & IMPROVISATIONAL IN NATURE, RHAPSODY'). Treat the final item after the clue as the archived answer and copy it, ignoring the surrounding noisy passages.
